classification.difficultyReason: Interpret coincident journeys and return times, compare simultaneous distances to locate the greatest separation, and use the first two hours' travelled distance to calculate average speed.

content.prompt: Two friends start off together from their holiday flat to go for a long walk. They both walk along a pathway and return to the flat on the same pathway.

spec.description: Two piecewise-linear journeys, with direct series labels, diamond and square markers, dashed reading guides, all printed ticks and the unlabelled final horizontal tick.

mathematics.horizontalAxis: Time (hours), labelled 0–6; final unlabelled tick at 7

spec.answerVisibility: All supplied graph data remain visible in the question edition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: For how long did the two friends walk together?

answer.worked: Their graphs coincide from 0 to 1 hour, so they walked together for 1 hour.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the greatest distance along the pathway that Bita was from the flat?

answer.worked: The highest point on Bita’s graph is at 6 km from the flat.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How long did Christina walk for?

answer.worked: Christina starts at 0 hours and returns to the flat at 5 hours, with no horizontal stopping segment. She walks for 5 hours.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What was the greatest distance apart of the two friends?

answer.worked:
The greatest vertical separation occurs after 4 hours. Bita is 5.5 km from the flat and Christina is 3 km from the flat.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance apart}&=5.5-3\\\text{Distance apart}&=2.5\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: What was Christina’s average walking speed for the first 2 hours?

answer.worked:
Christina travels 5 km in the first 2 hours.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Average speed}&=\frac{\text{distance travelled}}{\text{time taken}}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{5}{2}\\\text{Average speed}&=2.5\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$
